claims.text: Increasing chromium content in steel enhances the formation and stability of a passivating oxide layer at high temperature and pressure.
The chromium-enhanced passivating layer reduces corrosion in chemical-processing and nuclear-reactor environments.
Chromium contents of 9–18% are typical of the stainless-steel range relevant to the proposed study.
A high-temperature, pressurized aqueous environment containing chloride and lithium hydroxide can represent chemical-processing and nuclear conditions while remaining neutral or slightly alkaline.
A static aqueous autoclave corrosion test at 11.3 MPa and 320 °C with oxygen below 10 ppm is an established exposure protocol.
Repeated exposure and sampling at cumulative durations of 20, 40, and 60 days can be used to track corrosion evolution.
The governing structural mediator is a chromium-enriched oxide film formed on the steel surface.
A Cr2O3-rich passivation layer limits oxygen and aggressive-ion transport between the environment and the underlying steel.
Limiting oxygen and aggressive-ion transport reduces metal dissolution.
Higher-chromium steels will exhibit larger charge-transfer resistance than lower-chromium steels under otherwise identical conditions.
Higher-chromium steels will exhibit lower corrosion current densities than lower-chromium steels under otherwise identical conditions.
Higher-chromium steels will develop more continuous, uniform, chromium-rich oxide layers after repeated exposure.
A low-alloy steel containing no more than 5% chromium will have a higher corrosion rate and a less protective oxide than the higher-chromium steels.
The proposed mechanism applies across ferritic, martensitic, and austenitic steels containing 9–18% chromium in pressurized high-temperature water.
Extreme acidic or extremely oxidizing conditions fall outside the range in which the proposed chromium-passivation mechanism is expected to hold.
Nickel, molybdenum, microstructure, and local pH can influence the measured corrosion response independently of chromium content.
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and potentiodynamic polarization are applicable corrosion-measurement methods in chloride solution.

contradictions.description: The principal baseline is defined as steel with no more than 5% Cr, but the stated validity boundary begins at 9% Cr. Thus, the central baseline comparison lies outside the hypothesis's declared compositional domain.
